unit_test_finding.headline: THE SUBJECT'S OWN UNIT SUITE WAS RED, AND THE TEST WAS ASSERTING SOMETHING FALSE.

first_run.panic: to_mir.rs:23704: `body should be inside the multi-block marker class`

unit_test_finding.root_cause: the test asked `clamp_u32(swap = true)` — the corpus body with the comparison's operands exchanged, so the CAST is leftmost — to be ADMITTED with an empty delay set. It is not admitted. That body's comparison result IS the `CondBr` condition and therefore MARKED, and ORDERING RULE (1) (a marked result may not take a marked operand) refuses the whole body. Rule (1) is lane K's, unchanged by this lane, and it already refuses this shape at HEAD — so the test's own comment (`bodies in that shape FLIP today`) was false as well.
unit_test_finding.why_it_did_not_show_up_in_the_whole_crat: the corpus body is `clamp_u32(swap = false)`, the NON-leftmost order, which is admitted and delayed and is one of the two bodies this lane converts. The failing test is about the leftmost twin, which the corpus does not contain.

repair.what: the false assertion is replaced by THREE tests, and the claim it meant to pin — the delay is taken at a non-leftmost operand position and nowhere else — is pinned in a body the plan ACCEPTS in both orders (`arm_cast`, whose comparison flows into a `Br` edge argument and is therefore unmarked, keeping rule (1) out of the question)
tests: the_same_admitted_body_with_the_cast_non_leftmost_is_delayed — ADMITTED, delay set {v6}; one operand apart from the first, same instructions, same block graph, same marked set
a_leftmost_cast_under_a_marked_consumer_is_refused_by_ordering_rule_one — the ORIGINAL fixture, now asserting the refusal that actually happens and naming the rule
repair.strictly_stronger: the old test made ONE assertion that could not hold; the three make four that do, and they separate the delay's condition from rule (1)'s refusal instead of conflating them
repair.the_sealed_driver_is_UNAFFECTED_and_that: the whole repair lies in old lines 23901-23908 of `to_mir.rs`, inside `#[cfg(test)] mod branch_marker_plan_tests` (lines 23630-24035). Everything before 23901 and everything after 23908 is byte-identical. `cargo build --release` does not compile `cfg(test)` code, so the SEALED subject driver — built from the pre-repair file and the source of every whole-crate number in this artifact — compiles the same non-test source the repaired file does. No re-seal, and no number here moves.
